concerns.text: SC-004 (memory‑usage limit) is not anchored to any user story; it only references the Edge Cases section. Every Success Criterion must trace back to a concrete user story (US‑1, US‑2, or US‑3).

FR-013 specifies a linear mixed‑effects regression with random intercepts for participant ID, but the merged dataset is cross‑sectional (each participant appears only once). Random intercepts are therefore non‑identifiable and add no statistical value, contradicting the data structure implied by US‑1 and the edge‑case description.

FR-001 requires a data merge with ≥ 80 % overlap of AGP participant IDs with HRS IDs. Publicly available AGP and HRS datasets have no shared participant identifier, making the required overlap impossible to achieve; the requirement cannot be satisfied nor verified.
SC-001 mirrors the impossible ≥ 80 % overlap condition from FR-001, so the success criterion is untestable because the underlying data linkage cannot occur.

FR-013 specifies a linear mixed‑effects regression with random intercepts for participant ID, yet each participant appears only once after the merge (cross‑sectional design). Random intercepts are non‑identifiable, causing the model to fail to fit; the requirement is therefore not verifiable.

FR-005 states a sensitivity analysis “sweeping the rarefaction depth threshold over the set `{5,000, min_depth}` in steps of multiple reads” without defining the step size or what constitutes “multiple reads,” leaving the procedure ambiguous and not directly reproducible.

The specification assumes that the American Gut Project (AGP) and the Health and Retirement Study (HRS) can be merged by a shared participant identifier (US‑1 acceptance scenario ‘≥ 80 % overlap on participant IDs’). Publicly available AGP and HRS datasets have no common identifier; participants in AGP did not take the HRS cognitive module. This makes the core data‑integration premise infeasible, invalidating any downstream association analysis.

FR‑013 calls for a linear mixed‑effects regression with random intercepts for participant ID, yet each participant appears only once after the merge (cross‑sectional design). Random intercepts are non‑identifiable and add no statistical value, constituting a mis‑specified model. The analysis should use a standard linear regression (or a mixed model only if repeated measures exist).

responses.response: Anchored SC-004 to User Story US-3 and clarified the memory‑usage target.

responses.what_changed: Rewrote FR-013 to specify ordinary least‑squares regression (no random effects).

responses.what_changed: FR-001 now requires ≥ 200 linked participants via probabilistic record linkage; updated acceptance scenario accordingly.

responses.what_changed: SC-001 now requires ≥ 200 linked participants (See US-1).

responses.response: Made FR-013 testable by using a standard linear regression model.

responses.response: Specified concrete step size for the rarefaction depth sweep.
responses.what_changed: FR-005 now sweeps depth from 5,000 to min_depth in increments of 500 reads.

responses.what_changed: Rewrote relevant sentences in US-1, FR-001, and Assumptions to reflect demographic‑based probabilistic linkage; eliminated contradictory statements.
